scope: Per-game independent supervisor, Forge closure/crash survival and session recovery
covered_cases: Client detach and reattachment preserve supervisor, game and host
SIGKILL of a disposable UI parent leaves its supervisor and game recoverable
Duplicate supervised launches rejected by locks and live session identity
Normal game exit stops host and removes socket even without UI
Cancellation during preparation and failed game spawn clean up
Cancellation after spawn does not terminate the game
Immediate and nonzero exits remain available to late observers after another launch
Host loss retains the running game reservation
Supervisor loss retains guards for the exact surviving game process
Kernel identity mismatch prevents PID reuse from restoring a stale game
Corrupt metadata and unknown running identity keep operations blocked
Native helper returns and flushes kernel process identity before _exit
Swift recovery blocks operations before its first await and retries control failures
Recovered Swift model displays Running and blocks relaunch, verification and uninstall until exit
Cancelled UI observation still waits for actual recovered session completion

validation_limits.process_fixtures: Disposable sleep/true/false game processes and a pipe-owned shell host; production supervisor, IPC, lock and runtime cleanup code. Platform identity uses a test adapter; native libproc and helper transport are tested separately.
